Test Step 6 of the SFCC-236 build — the FINAL, most consequential step: `ZimmProductCard` organism. Files:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCard.css.ts}
- overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts (1 import + 1 registry entry)

## What this organism is
Composes ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) + ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) into the actual shared product card. Owns a discriminated union (`variation: 'plp'|'home'|'wishlist'`) and a `VARIATION_CONFIG` object driving all show/hide logic — the render body must contain ZERO `switch`/`if` on `props.variation`. Also owns the "stretched-link" pattern: Content's `nameLink` is the ONLY real `<a>` in the whole composed tree, and this organism's own recipe adds a `::after` overlay to it (via a `[data-card-slot="content"] a::after` descendant selector) so clicking anywhere on the card navigates to the PDP, while bag/arrows/size-chips/remove stay independently clickable via `position:relative; zIndex:1`.

## CRITICAL CONTEXT — the Implementer explicitly flagged its own biggest limitation, verify this is genuinely closed or still open
The Implementer had NO Figma tool access this session and could not independently verify some cited nodes. It also explicitly stated in its own report: "jsdom does no layout/paint/hit-testing — fireEvent/user-event dispatch straight to the named node regardless of what a browser's stacking-order hit-test would actually resolve... going from [passing interaction tests] to 'a real click lands correctly' is exactly what a real-browser check is for, and this step has not done that check." This is the single most important open item — your interaction-test review should explicitly assess whether the SHIPPED tests could pass even if the real CSS z-index/stacking were broken (i.e., are they testing the DOM/callback wiring only, or do they somehow also validate real hit-testing — they cannot, in jsdom, so confirm this limitation is real and clearly state it, don't let a "26/26 passed" summary imply more than it does).

## Required verification — read the actual files, don't trust the report

1. **The union enforcement.** Read the actual type definitions in `index.tsx`. The Implementer reports exporting `ZimmProductCardBaseProps`/`ZimmProductCardPlpVariation`/`ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`/`ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` (deviating from an original "keep them private" sketch) because "excess-property checking against a union type is weak — assigning a fresh object literal with an extra field belonging to a DIFFERENT union member doesn't get flagged." Verify this claim is real TypeScript behaviour (it is a known, documented TS quirk — confirm the test file's actual `@ts-expect-error` cases are constructed in a way that genuinely triggers a real compile error, not a vacuous one). Falsify this: temporarily remove one `@ts-expect-error` comment, run `tsc`, confirm it now reports an actual usable/expected error (proving the expect-error was doing real work), then revert.

2. **No `switch`/`if` on `variation` in the render body.** Grep `index.tsx` yourself for `variation ===`, `switch (variation)`, `switch(props.variation)`, etc. Confirm zero hits in the actual render/JSX logic (some hits in type definitions or the VARIATION_CONFIG object's own keys are fine and expected — distinguish those from actual branching logic).

3. **VARIATION_CONFIG accuracy against the CONFIRMED matrix** (already verified via Figma `hidden` attributes earlier in this build, treat this table as ground truth, not something to re-derive):
   - Home: showBag=false, showAttributes=false, showSizeChips=false, hoverRevealsPrice=true, hoverHidesPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=false.
   - PLP: showBag=true, showAttributes=false, showSizeChips=true, hoverHidesPrice=true, hoverRevealsPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=true.
   - Wishlist: showBag=true, showAttributes=true, showSizeChips=true, hoverHidesPrice=true, hoverRevealsPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=true, showRemove=true.
   Read the actual `VARIATION_CONFIG` object in the code and confirm it matches this exactly, cell by cell.

4. **Exactly one `<a>` per card, in every variation.** Read the test asserting this; also verify by reading the actual composition in `index.tsx` that Media is never given its own separate link/anchor anywhere.

5. **The stretched-link CSS itself** — read `zimmProductCard.css.ts` in full. Confirm: `root` is `position:relative`; the `::after` overlay selector targets `[data-card-slot="content"] a::after` with `inset:0`; the lift selectors (`[data-card-slot="close"]`, `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button`, `[data-card-slot="content"] button`) all get `position:relative; zIndex:1`. Confirm size chips are ALSO covered by a lift selector — the brief required "every size chip" to remain clickable, check whether `[data-card-slot="content"] button` actually reaches size chip buttons (are size chips rendered as `<button>` elements? check `ZimmSizeChip`'s own root element) or whether they need a separate, more specific selector that might be missing.

6. **The Stylis compile-time verification claim.** The Implementer reports writing "a throwaway Node script (not committed)" that compiled the actual selectors through the project's real installed Stylis engine to confirm they scope correctly. This is not independently re-checkable by you unless you rerun something similar — note this as accepted-on-report if you don't have a way to verify it yourself, but flag it as such rather than silently treating it as equivalent to your own verification.

7. **Two deviations to sanity-check:**
   - `showNotifyMe` computed as `Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe)` uniformly across ALL THREE variations (not restricted to PLP), because `onNotifyMe` sits on the shared base props type. Is this a reasonable interpretation, or does it risk producing a Home/Wishlist card that unexpectedly shows a notify-me link when a caller passes `isUnavailable` + `onNotifyMe` for a variation the AC never intended this for? Check whether this is actually reachable/dangerous or purely theoretical (i.e., would SFCC-90/497's future organism-callers realistically ever pass both props for a Home/Wishlist card?).
   - No `priority` prop passthrough to Media's LCP escape hatch — confirmed absent, flagged as a known gap in the file's own docblock rather than silently dropped. Just confirm the docblock genuinely says this, don't let it be an undocumented silent omission.

## Falsification requirements — the highest-value ones for THIS step
(a) The `@ts-expect-error` removal test described in point 1 above.
(b) Break the stretched-link overlay on purpose — e.g. temporarily give the overlay a `zIndex: 10` (higher than the lift selectors' `zIndex: 1`) in the real recipe, rerun the interaction tests, and see whether ANY of them fail. Given the Implementer's own honest caveat that jsdom can't hit-test, my strong expectation is that NOTHING fails — if that's what you find, that CONFIRMS the interaction tests provide zero protection against this exact class of regression, which is important, real information to report clearly (not a contradiction of the Implementer's work, a confirmation of their own stated limitation). Revert after.
(c) Pick one interaction test (e.g. the bag-click test) and read exactly what DOM query it uses to find the bag button — confirm it's finding the real, actually-rendered button from the real composed Media/Content tree (not a mocked stand-in that would trivially "pass" regardless of the real component's structure).

## Commands to run yourself
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
Baseline going into this step: 51 files / 793 tests. Implementer claims 52 files / 820 tests (793 + 26 own tests + 1 recipeParts growth = 820, confirm this reconciliation).

Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings, UNIFORM vs ONE-OFF, what you falsified, what you could not verify. Be explicit and honest about the real-browser-click gap — that is the single most important thing for this report to get right, more than any individual code nit.

CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (today), pattern is UNIFORM risk (see below).** The organism's lift rule: ```ts '[data-card-slot="close"]': { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 }, ``` compiles (verified by a full real render — see falsification (b) below) to `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]{position:relative;z-index:1;}` — a class + attribute-selector descendant combinator, specificity `(0,2,0)`. Media's own `close` part (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:111-116`) sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on a single class, specificity `(0,1,0)`. The organism's rule wins the `position` cascade for that property, so **the real, computed style of the remove button is `position: relative`, not `absolute`.** `top:0; right:0` survive but are now a no-op relative offset — the button renders in normal document flow (after the image scroll container) instead of pinned over the image's top-right corner, for every Wishlist card, unconditionally. I verified this empirically, not just by specificity arithmetic: rendered the organism with the **real** `ChakraProvider`/theme/recipes (no `useMultiStyleConfig` mock) for `variation="wishlist"` and read `getComputedStyle`: ``` CLOSE computed position/top/right/zIndex: relative 0px 0px 1 BAG computed position/zIndex: relative 1 ARROW computed position/zIndex: relative 1 CAROUSEL WRAPPER computed position: absolute 50% size-chip[0..1] position/zIndex: relative 1 (both) ``` Bag/arrow/size-chip buttons are all correctly and non-destructively lifted (none of them had a prior conflicting `position`, so `position:relative` is a safe no-op there). **`close` is the one control that was already independently `position:absolute` in its own component recipe, and it's the one control the lift rule breaks.** Storybook uses this exact real theme (`.storybook/preview.tsx` imports `overrides/app/theme`), so the `Wishlist` story will show this today — no hover needed, no interaction needed, visible on first paint. This directly contradicts the recipe's own docblock intent ("LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay... position:relative plus a z-index higher than the overlay's own") — `position:relative` was never necessary here for z-index purposes (an already-`absolute` element is already positioned; only `zIndex:1` was needed), and adding it destroys the layout. *Why "UNIFORM risk" despite being ONE-OFF today:* the same broad `[data-card-slot="X"] button`-style lift-selector pattern will silently break any *future* control added under one of these three lift targets that needs its own `position: absolute/fixed` (a future badge-dismiss button, a "quick view" overlay, etc.) — the mechanism has no guard against this recurring. **Recipe state exhaustiveness — mostly dropped as vacuous for this file.** The organism's recipe declares one part (`root`), and `root` itself has no `onClick`/keyboard handling of its own — it isn't a Figma-stateful interactive part, it's a pure hover-reveal/z-index composition surface.
